children: Singapore disagrees with the U.S. Trade Representative office's findings and is 'very disappointed with the proposed actions' against the city-state, the island-nation's Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry said.
The ministry will continue to engage its U.S. counterpart, and urge the USTR to reconsider its proposed actions on Singapore and explore ways to reduce the tariff, it said Thursday.

The ministry's comments came after the U.S. proposed new tariffs on China and dozens of other countries, including Singapore. The Trump administration said that these countries are harming American companies by supporting their own domestic industrial production.
The U.S. is proposing a 20% tariff on most Chinese products, which would be added to Trump's first-term tariffs and could rise to 40% if negotiations between the two nations collapse.
Tariffs on other U.S. trading partners would also rise under the action, but wouldn't exceed levels that the Trump administration and foreign governments agreed to in a series of trade deals in 2025.

title: Singapore 'Very Disappointed' With Proposed U.S. Tariffs
